history.origins: Fish Pitch is a partnership Pitch variation contributed by Judd A. Schorr and documented in published card-game rules. It belongs to the Pitch/Setback family, which is North American and derived from the English game of All Fours (Seven Up). Pitch added bidding to All Fours; partnership forms became popular in the American mid-west as family or social games. Fish Pitch adds a fishing mechanic where each player has six hand cards and six face-down cards from which they may play during tricks, creating uncertainty and limiting card-counting.
timeline: 20th century: Documented as a Pitch variation with fishing mechanic; rules contributed by Judd A. Schorr.

setup.dealing: Each player receives six cards, dealt three at a time.

rules.objective: The pitcher leads a card to the first trick, and the suit of this card becomes the trump suit.
